Upload your syllabi; get the semester back as an app — every deadline with the sentence it came from, a study guide you can drill, narrated lessons, a deck, a document, and a calendar that knows when your classes are.
Built first for one Vanderbilt semester (Fall 2026, four courses, by hand), then generalised: anyone can sign in, upload their own syllabus and readings, and get the same thing for their own courses.

requirements.text: Built first for one Vanderbilt semester (Fall 2026, four courses, by hand), then generalised: anyone can sign in, upload their own syllabus and readings, and get the same thing for their own courses.

Accounts live in Supabase, and the two values the app needs to find it are committed in app/.env.production — both are public by design, and what protects an account is the row-level policy on every table, not the secrecy of a key that ships inside the page.

Apple is a third case, and the screen says which half is which: iCloud calendars come in with no account and no key — publish one from the Calendar app and paste the webcal:// link — while Sign in with Apple gives identity only, and needs a paid developer account, an https redirect (Apple rejects localhost) and the dev server to sign its client secret.
